description: Estimate cycling power in watts from speed, rider weight, and gradient using the standard physics model.

faqs.a: Power overcomes three resistances: aerodynamic drag, rolling resistance, and gravity on hills. The model sums all three.
Flat-road cruising is usually 100–200 W, a strong club rider holds 250–300 W, and pros exceed 400 W on climbs.
An estimate only — it cannot replace a power meter. Wind, position, and tires change real values by 10–20%.
faqs.q: Is this as accurate as a power meter?

howto: Enter your average speed in km/h.
Enter rider weight and bike weight in kg.
Enter the average gradient in percent (negative for descents).
Press Calculate to see estimated watts and the breakdown.
title: Cycling Power Estimator
